title: Load Balancer
body:
The machine that sits at the front of a company's infrastructure, receives incoming connections, and distributes them across a pool of backend application servers. In the postal analogy it's the front desk: the letter arrives there, and the front desk decides which department gets it.

Several things people assume happen "at the server" actually happen here: the [[TCP Three-Way Handshake]] usually terminates at the load balancer, and so does the [[TLS Handshake]] (called TLS termination). It's also the source of **502 Bad Gateway** — that status means the load balancer itself got an invalid response from one of the app servers behind it, which is a useful diagnostic because it tells you the request reached their infrastructure and failed *inside* it. A reverse proxy is the same idea framed as request routing rather than distribution; in practice the same software (nginx, HAProxy, an ALB) does both.
